events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Cottonwood Burn Scar in...
West Central Piute County in central Utah...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

* At 114 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County. Between
0.25 and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen, with the heaviest rainfall
occurring over Gold Gulch and Ten Mile Creek areas. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through the Gold Gulch and Ten Mile Creek, and possibly
Cottonwood Gulch. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials. These debris flows are
expected to travel downstream impacting HW 89 between mile markers
171 to 176.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Cottonwood Burn Scar in
Piute County, with flows impacting US 89 between mile
markers 171 to 176.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
US 89 between mile markers 171 to 176 in.

FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Southwestern Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...
West Central Washington County in southeastern Ohio...

* Until 615 PM EDT.

* At 306 PM EDT, Even though heavy rainfall has ended for now,
continued runoff will result in flash flooding of creeks and
streams. Additionally, thunderstorms may move back into the area
late this afternoon, further exacerbating the flooding situation.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. This area received between 3
to 4 inches from since midnight and is particularly
vulnerable to additional heavy rainfall. People should
remain vigilant into the early evening hours for
additional rises of creeks and streams.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chesterhill, Amesville, Bartlett and Fleming.
